newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Japanese oil groups reported in petrol tie-up.
newsitem.headline: Two Japanese oil groups reported in petrol tie-up.

text.p: Japan's two-largest oil wholesalers have agreed to link their distribution networks to better cope with competition that has come with the deregulation of the industry, a Japanese newspaper reported on Saturday.
The report, in the Daily Yomiuri newspaper, quoted an industry source as saying that Nippon Oil Co and Idemitsu Kosan Co would merge their oil tank operations and standardise petrol quality.

The report said that the companies hoped to reduce distribution costs as outside retailers such as supermarkets enter the petrol business. The oil tank bases are used to hold oil products before they are trucked to retailers.
The move, to start in April, was also expected to put pressure on other oil wholesalers.
Nippon Oil has 86 oil tank bases nationwide, while Idemitsu has 34.
The two companies have already teamed up in other oil products, including kerosene and motor oil.
Distribution companies have been under pressure from a drop in retail prices for petrol since the liberalisation of oil imports last April.
